# Royal Rose Crest (#31)

Owner, 2026-11-19: "a theme similar to the royal olive one, but pink (rose gold or baby pink) with a matching set for
the gold; fill in the crest; use the textures (the green-gold damask) recoloured to match."

The owner was shown four colourings of Royal Olive Crest (blush & rose gold, baby pink & rose gold, baby pink &
champagne gold, dusty rose & antique gold) and chose **B, baby pink & rose gold**, the crest **filled, with the
couple's initials engraved**, and **the damask and the floral scroll** as backgrounds.

## Artwork

Every picture in `v1/assets` is Royal Olive Crest v3's, recoloured by gradient-mapping each colour family's
lightness onto the new palette, so the gold's highlights and the paper grain are kept:

| Royal Olive | Royal Rose (B) |
|---|---|
| olive panels | baby pink `#c58796 → #efc0cb → #fde6ec` |
| gold | rose gold `#4f241c → #94503f → #d1907a → #f6d3c4` |
| cream paper | blush cream `#cdb6b2 → #fff6f5` |

Every crest's shield (empty in Royal Olive) is filled with pink enamel: lighter at the top, a faint damask, darker
towards the rim. The initials are not in the pictures: the design writes them (the wax seal's letters) over each
shield, on the invitation and on every printed piece, so they follow the customer's names.

Textures (the owner's slides, 2026-11-19), recoloured: `damask.webp` (the green-gold damask, a seamless tile, behind
the pages) and `scroll.webp` (the floral scroll from the brown and burgundy slides, behind the crest page, the envelope
and the closing).

The printed A5 card no longer prints the invitation's paragraph (house rule; Royal Olive v3 still does).
